questions.text: समजात अंग इंगित करते हैं :
questions.text_english: Homologous organs indicate :
questions.solution: Homologous organs are those that have the same basic structural plan and origin but may perform different functions in different organisms, such as the forelimbs of a whale, bat, cheetah and human. Because these organs arise from a common ancestor but have diversified in structure and function as organisms adapted to different environments, they are evidence of Divergent Evolution (option B). Convergent evolution produces analogous organs (similar function, different origin), not homologous ones. Adaptive radiation is a related concept but refers to the process of diversification from a common ancestor, while Divergent Evolution is the precise term indicated by homologous structures.
questions.solution_hindi: समजात अंग वे होते हैं जिनकी मूल संरचना एवं उत्पत्ति समान होती है लेकिन वे विभिन्न जीवों में अलग-अलग कार्य करते हैं। जैसे व्हेल, चमगादड़, चीता और मानव के अग्रपाद। ये अपसारी विकास के प्रमाण हैं।

questions.text: 2 युग्मविकल्पी (दो विशेषकों) वाले जीन के लिए एक समष्टि आनुवंशिक संतुलन/हार्डी-वेनबर्ग संतुलन में होती है (प्रभावी ऐलील 'A' तथा अप्रभावी ऐलील 'a' है)। यदि ऐलील 'A' की आवृत्ति 0·6 है, तो जीनोटाइप 'Aa' की आवृत्ति होगी :
questions.text_english: A population is in genetic equilibrium/Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with 2 alleles (dominant allele is 'A' and recessive allele 'a'). If the frequency of allele 'A' is 0·6, then the frequency of genotype 'Aa' is :
questions.solution: According to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, if p = frequency of allele A = 0.6, then q = frequency of allele a = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4. The frequency of heterozygous genotype Aa = 2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48. Therefore option C (0.48) is correct. Option A (0.21) would be p² if p were 0.46. Option B (0.42) is incorrect. Option D (0.32) = q² × 2 which is not a standard formula.

questions.text: डीएनए अणु की द्विकुंडली संरचना में, रज्जुक होते हैं :
questions.text_english: In the double helical structure of DNA molecule, the strands are :
questions.solution: In the Watson-Crick double helix model of DNA, the two strands are anti-parallel (one runs 5'→3' and the other runs 3'→5') and complementary (A pairs with T and G pairs with C via hydrogen bonds). They are not identical because one strand is the complement of the other. Option C is therefore correct. Options A and B are wrong because the strands are not identical. Option D is wrong because the strands are indeed complementary.
questions.solution_hindi: डीएनए की द्विकुंडली संरचना में दोनों रज्जुक प्रति-समानांतर (anti-parallel) होते हैं तथा पूरक (complementary) भी होते हैं — A, T के साथ और G, C के साथ जुड़ता है।

questions.text: एक 'अनुलेखन इकाई' में, 'समापक' (टर्मीनेटर) इस ओर अवस्थित होता है :
questions.text_english: In a 'transcription unit', the 'terminator' is located towards the :
questions.solution: In a transcription unit, transcription proceeds from the promoter (located at the 3' end of the template strand) towards the terminator (located at the 5' end of the template strand). Since the template strand is read 3'→5', the terminator lies at the 5' end of the template strand. On the coding (non-template) strand, this corresponds to the 3' end. Therefore option B is correct. The terminator signals RNA polymerase to stop transcription.
questions.solution_hindi: अनुलेखन इकाई में, टर्मीनेटर टेम्पलेट रज्जुक के 5' किनारे पर अवस्थित होता है। यह RNA पॉलीमरेज़ को अनुलेखन रोकने का संकेत देता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प मानव वंशावली विश्लेषण में समरक्त मैथुन (रिश्तेदारों के बीच मैथुन) को दर्शाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following option denotes mating between relatives in human pedigree analysis ?

options.A: Circle connected to square by a single horizontal line
options.B: Circle connected to square by a double line with a diagonal line through the square
options.C: Circle connected to a hatched square
options.D: Circle connected to square by a double horizontal line

options_english.A: Circle connected to square by a single horizontal line
options_english.B: Circle connected to square by a double line with a diagonal
options_english.C: Circle connected to a hatched square
options_english.D: Circle connected to square by a double horizontal line

questions.solution: In human pedigree analysis, a double horizontal line between a circle (female) and a square (male) denotes a consanguineous mating, i.e., mating between relatives. This is the standard convention used in genetics. Option A shows a normal unrelated mating. Option B shows mating with a deceased individual. Option C shows mating with an affected individual. Option D (double line) is the correct symbol for consanguineous mating.
questions.solution_hindi: वंशावली विश्लेषण में, दोहरी क्षैतिज रेखा से जुड़े वृत्त (मादा) और वर्ग (नर) समरक्त मैथुन (रिश्तेदारों के बीच) को दर्शाते हैं।

questions.text: डेंगू ज्वर का संवाहक है :
questions.text_english: The vector for dengue fever is :
questions.solution: Dengue fever is transmitted by the female Aedes mosquito (specifically Aedes aegypti). Only female mosquitoes bite and feed on blood, making them vectors for pathogens. Male mosquitoes feed only on plant nectar. Female Anopheles mosquito transmits malaria, female Culex transmits filariasis. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: डेंगू ज्वर का संवाहक मादा एडीज़ मच्छर है। मादा एनोफेलीज़ मलेरिया और मादा क्यूलेक्स फाइलेरिया का संवाहक है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जोड़ों में से कौन-सा सही सुमेलित नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
questions.solution: Monascus purpureus is a fungus used to produce statins (blood cholesterol-lowering agents), not citric acid. Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger. Therefore option C is incorrectly matched and is the correct answer. Options A, B, and D are all correctly matched: Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid, Trichoderma polysporum produces the immunosuppressant Cyclosporin A, and Streptococcus produces Streptokinase (a clot-busting enzyme).
questions.solution_hindi: मोनैस्कस परप्यूरीअस स्टेटिन (रक्त कोलेस्ट्रॉल घटाने वाला) उत्पन्न करता है, सिट्रिक अम्ल नहीं। सिट्रिक अम्ल एस्परजिलस नाइजर द्वारा उत्पन्न होता है। अतः विकल्प C गलत सुमेलित है।

questions.text: पीसीआर के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किसकी आवश्यकता नहीं होती ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not required for PCR ?
questions.solution: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) requires: a DNA template (DNA segment), primers (short oligonucleotides that flank the target sequence), Taq polymerase (a heat-stable DNA polymerase from Thermus aquaticus), and deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs). Restriction endonuclease is used for cutting DNA at specific sites in recombinant DNA technology, but it is NOT required in the PCR process itself. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: PCR के लिए DNA खंड, प्राइमर, टैक पॉलिमरेज़ और dNTPs की आवश्यकता होती है। प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ की PCR में कोई आवश्यकता नहीं होती — यह पुनर्योगज DNA तकनीक में प्रयुक्त होती है।

questions.text: समुद्र में जैवमात्रा का पिरामिड सामान्यतः उल्टा होता है क्योंकि समुद्र में :
questions.text_english: The pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted because in sea :

options.A: मछलियों की जैवमात्रा पादपप्लवकों की अपेक्षा अधिक होती है।
options.B: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत अधिक होती है।
options.C: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत कम होती है।
options.D: बड़ी मछलियाँ छोटी मछलियों को खाती हैं।

options_english.A: Biomass of fishes exceeds that of phytoplankton.
options_english.D: Large fishes feed on small fishes.

questions.solution: In a marine ecosystem, the pyramid of biomass is inverted because at any given time the biomass of fishes (consumers) is greater than that of phytoplankton (producers). This happens because phytoplankton have a very rapid turnover rate — they reproduce and are consumed very quickly, so their standing crop biomass is low at any instant, even though their productivity is high. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: समुद्र में जैवमात्रा का पिरामिड उल्टा होता है क्योंकि किसी भी समय मछलियों की जैवमात्रा पादपप्लवकों (उत्पादकों) की जैवमात्रा से अधिक होती है, क्योंकि पादपप्लवक बहुत तेज़ी से उपभोग होते हैं।

questions.text: मानव में, द्वितीयक अंडक का अर्धसूत्री विभाजन तब पूर्ण होता है जब :
questions.text_english: In humans, the secondary oocyte completes meiotic division when :

options.A: यह गर्भाशय के अंत:स्तर में अंतरोपित हो जाता है।
options.B: यह परिपक्व ग्राफी पुटक से मोचित होता है।
options.D: अग्रपिंडक के एंज़ाइम ज़ोना पेलुसिडा (पारदर्शी अंडावरण) का भंजन करते हैं।

options_english.A: it gets implanted in the uterine endometrium.
options_english.B: it is released from the matured Graafian follicle.
options_english.C: it is penetrated by the sperm cell.
options_english.D: acrosomal enzymes break down the zona pellucida.

questions.solution: The secondary oocyte is arrested at Metaphase II of meiosis. It completes the second meiotic division only after a sperm cell penetrates it during fertilization, triggering the resumption of meiosis II and producing the ovum (egg cell) and a second polar body. It is not completed at ovulation (when it is released from the Graafian follicle) — at that stage it is still a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II. Therefore option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीयक अंडक अर्धसूत्री विभाजन II की मेटाफेज अवस्था में रुका रहता है। शुक्राणु के प्रवेश करने पर ही यह विभाजन पूर्ण होता है और अंडाणु तथा द्वितीय ध्रुवीय काय बनती है।

questions.text:
स्तंभ I की मदों का मिलान स्तंभ II से कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही सुमेलित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
स्तंभ I (क्रॉस): 1. मेंडलीय एकसंकर (मोनोहाइब्रिड), 2. मेंडलीय द्विसंकर, 3. अपूर्ण प्रभाविता (इंकंप्लीट डोमिनेंस), 4. परीक्षार्थ संकरण (एकसंकर) (मोनोहाइब्रिड)
स्तंभ II (फिनोटाइप (दृश्यरूप) अनुपात): (i) 1:2:1 (F2), (ii) 1:1, (iii) 3:1 (F2), (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.text_english:
Match the items in Column I with those in Column II and select the correctly matched option:
Column I (Cross): 1. Mendelian monohybrid, 2. Mendelian dihybrid, 3. Incomplete dominance, 4. Test cross (monohybrid)
Column II (Phenotypic Ratio): (i) 1:2:1 (F2), (ii) 1:1, (iii) 3:1 (F2), (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.solution: The correct matching is: Mendelian monohybrid F2 gives 3:1 phenotypic ratio (iii); Mendelian dihybrid F2 gives 9:3:3:1 (iv); Incomplete dominance F2 gives 1:2:1 (i) because the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype; Test cross (monohybrid) gives 1:1 (ii) because crossing the unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive gives either all dominant phenotype or 1:1. Therefore option C (1-iii, 2-iv, 3-i, 4-ii) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: मेंडलीय एकसंकर F2 = 3:1 (iii); मेंडलीय द्विसंकर F2 = 9:3:3:1 (iv); अपूर्ण प्रभाविता F2 = 1:2:1 (i); परीक्षार्थ संकरण = 1:1 (ii). अतः विकल्प C सही है।

questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी में कार्यशील गुरूबीजाणु विकसित होता है :
questions.text_english: The functional megaspore of an angiosperm develops into :
questions.solution: In angiosperms, megasporogenesis produces four megaspores from the megaspore mother cell. Of these, only one is functional (the chalazal megaspore in most species), and it undergoes three rounds of mitotic division to develop into the female gametophyte, which is the embryo sac (containing 7 cells and 8 nuclei, including the egg cell, synergids, central cell, and antipodal cells). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: आवृतबीजी में, कार्यशील गुरूबीजाणु तीन बार समसूत्री विभाजन करके भ्रूणकोश (7 कोशिकाएं, 8 केंद्रक) विकसित करता है, जो मादा युग्मकोद्भिद् है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): संसाधनों (प्राकृतिक संपदा) के अतिदोहन के कारण जैव-विविधता को क्षति पहुँच सकती है।
कारण (R): भारतीय नदियों में क्लैरियस गैरीपाइनस मछली को प्रविष्ट कराने के कारण भारतीय मूल की मछलियों की संख्या में कमी आ गई है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Loss of biodiversity can occur due to overexploitation of resources.
Reason (R): Introduction of Clarias gariepinus in Indian rivers has led to a decline in native Indian fishes.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं — जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Questions 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C), (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is true — overexploitation of natural resources is indeed one of the major causes of biodiversity loss. The Reason (R) is also true — introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus (an alien invasive species) into Indian rivers has caused a decline in native Indian fish populations. However, R is not the correct explanation of A, because R describes the impact of alien species introduction (a different cause of biodiversity loss), not overexploitation. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सत्य है — प्राकृतिक संसाधनों के अतिदोहन से जैव-विविधता की हानि होती है। R भी सत्य है — विदेशी मछली के प्रवेश से देशी मछलियाँ कम हुई हैं। लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है क्योंकि R विदेशी जाति के प्रवेश का प्रभाव बताता है, अतिदोहन का नहीं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): आनुवंशिक इंजीनियरिंग में, प्रतिजैविक जीनों का वरण-योग्य चिह्नक के रूप में उपयोग किया जाता है।
कारण (R): वरण-योग्य चिह्नक रूपांतरजों की अरूपांतरजों से पहचान करने में हमारी सहायता करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In genetic engineering, antibiotic genes are used as selectable markers.
Reason (R): Selectable markers help us to identify transformants from non-transformants.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are true and R correctly explains A. Antibiotic resistance genes (such as ampicillin resistance) are used as selectable markers in genetic engineering. When recombinant bacteria are plated on a medium containing the antibiotic, only the transformed cells (those that took up the plasmid with the antibiotic resistance gene) will survive. Thus, selectable markers like antibiotic genes help identify transformants from non-transformants. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सत्य है — प्रतिजैविक जीनों का वरण-योग्य चिह्नक के रूप में उपयोग होता है। R भी सत्य है और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है क्योंकि ये चिह्नक ही रूपांतरजों की पहचान में सहायक होते हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाएँ इन्टरफेरॉन उत्पन्न करती हैं।
कारण (R): इन्टरफेरॉन विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाओं में शोथ (जलन) उत्पन्न कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Virus-infected cells produce interferons.
Reason (R): Interferons can cause inflammation of virus-infected cells.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true — virus-infected cells do produce interferons as part of the innate immune response. Interferons are signalling proteins that warn neighbouring uninfected cells to activate antiviral defences. However, Reason (R) is false — interferons do not cause inflammation of virus-infected cells; rather, they protect uninfected cells from viral spread. Inflammation is caused by other immune mediators such as cytokines and histamines. Therefore option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सत्य है — विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाएँ इन्टरफेरॉन उत्पन्न करती हैं। R असत्य है — इन्टरफेरॉन शोथ उत्पन्न नहीं करते; वे अन्य कोशिकाओं को विषाणु से बचाते हैं।

अभिकथन (A): आरएनए अस्थायी है तथा तीव्र गति से उत्परिवर्तित हो सकता है।
कारण (R): आरएनए के प्रत्येक न्यूक्लियोटाइड में 2'–OH समूह की उपस्थिति इसे अस्थायी तथा सरलता से विघटित होने वाला बनाती है।

Assertion (A): RNA is unstable and can mutate at a faster rate.
Reason (R): The presence of 2'–OH group in every nucleotide of RNA makes it labile and easily degradable.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false.
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are true and R correctly explains A. RNA is indeed more unstable and mutates at a faster rate than DNA. The 2'–OH group present in every ribonucleotide of RNA makes the RNA molecule chemically reactive and more susceptible to hydrolysis (degradation) compared to DNA which lacks this hydroxyl group (it has H at the 2' position). This instability also means RNA can accumulate errors and mutate more readily. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सत्य है — RNA अस्थायी है और तेज़ी से उत्परिवर्तित होता है। R भी सत्य है और सही व्याख्या करता है — 2'–OH समूह RNA को अस्थायी और सहज विघटनशील बनाता है।

questions.text: अपरद की प्रकृति तथा ताप, अपघटन की दर को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करते हैं ?
questions.text_english: How is the rate of decomposition affected by the nature of detritus and temperature ?

key_points: Nature of detritus: Detritus rich in lignin, cellulose, and chitin decomposes slowly; detritus rich in water-soluble substances decomposes faster. The chemical composition (C:N ratio) affects rate.
Temperature: Higher temperature (up to an optimum) speeds up decomposition by increasing enzymatic activity of decomposers; very high or very low temperatures slow decomposition.

questions.solution: The rate of decomposition is influenced by both the nature of detritus and temperature. Detritus with a high proportion of lignin, cellulose, or chitin decomposes slowly because these are recalcitrant, complex organic molecules difficult for microbes to break down. Detritus rich in nitrogen and easily soluble compounds decomposes rapidly. Temperature plays a critical role because decomposition is primarily carried out by microbial enzymes — higher temperatures (up to an optimum of about 30–35°C) accelerate enzymatic activity and thus speed up decomposition, whereas very low temperatures reduce microbial activity and slow decomposition significantly.
questions.solution_hindi: अपरद में लिग्निन, सेलुलोज़ आदि की अधिकता होने पर अपघटन धीमा होता है। ताप बढ़ने से सूक्ष्मजीवों की एंज़ाइम क्रियाशीलता बढ़ती है और अपघटन तेज़ होता है; अत्यधिक कम ताप पर यह धीमा हो जाता है।

questions.text_english: How is a restriction endonuclease named ? Explain with the help of a suitable example.

key_points: Named after the organism from which it is isolated: first letter of genus (italicised capital), first two letters of species (italicised lower case), strain designation, and a Roman numeral for order of discovery.
Example: EcoRI — E from Escherichia, co from coli, R from strain RY13, I for first enzyme discovered from this strain.

questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases are named after the organism from which they are isolated, following a standard convention. The name consists of the first letter of the genus (in italics, capitalised), the first two letters of the species (in italics, lower case), the strain designation (if applicable), and a Roman numeral indicating the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that organism. For example, EcoRI: 'E' stands for the genus Escherichia, 'co' for the species coli, 'R' for the strain RY13, and 'I' indicates it was the first restriction enzyme isolated from this organism.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ का नाम उस जीव के नाम पर रखा जाता है जिससे इसे पृथक किया गया है। उदाहरण: EcoRI — 'E' Escherichia जीनस से, 'co' coli जाति से, 'R' प्रभेद RY13 से और 'I' इस जीव से पहला खोजा गया एंज़ाइम।

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name any two copper releasing intra-uterine devices. State two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

key_points: Two copper-releasing IUDs: CuT (Copper-T), Cu7, Multiload 375, Nova-T
Reason 1: Copper ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
Reason 2: They make the uterine endometrium unfavourable for implantation.

sub_questions.solution: Two copper-releasing intra-uterine devices are CuT (Copper-T) and Cu7 (or Multiload 375). They are effective contraceptives for two main reasons: first, the copper ions continuously released into the uterine cavity suppress sperm motility and reduce the fertilising capacity of sperms, thereby preventing fertilization; second, the physical presence of the device along with copper ions makes the uterine endometrium unsuitable for implantation of a fertilised egg, providing an additional contraceptive effect.

sub_questions.text: (ख) पुष्पीय पादपों द्वारा विकसित किन्हीं दो बहि:प्रजनन युक्तियों के नाम लिखिए तथा व्याख्या कीजिए कि परपरागण को प्रोत्साहित करने में वे किस प्रकार सहायक हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Name any two outbreeding devices that flowering plants have developed and explain how they help in encouraging cross-pollination.

key_points: Outbreeding devices: Dichogamy (protandry/protogyny), Herkogamy, Self-incompatibility, Unisexuality (monoecy/dioecy), Heterostyly
Each device prevents self-pollination and promotes cross-pollination by ensuring pollen and stigma of same flower are not functional at same time or are physically separated.

sub_questions.solution: Two outbreeding devices developed by flowering plants are dichogamy and self-incompatibility. In dichogamy, the anthers and stigma of the same flower mature at different times — if anthers mature first it is called protandry (e.g., sunflower), and if the stigma matures first it is called protogyny (e.g., Mirabilis). This prevents pollen from the same flower reaching the stigma when it is receptive, thereby promoting cross-pollination. Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents the germination of pollen from the same plant on its own stigma, thus forcing cross-pollination with pollen from another individual.

questions.text_english: Although Haemophilia and sickle cell anemia are two blood related Mendelian disorders, yet, they differ in their pattern of inheritance. State any two differences.

key_points: Haemophilia is X-linked recessive; Sickle cell anemia is autosomal recessive.
Haemophilia affects males more; females can be carriers. Sickle cell anemia affects both males and females equally.

questions.solution: The first difference is in the chromosomal location of the gene: Haemophilia is caused by a mutation in genes on the X chromosome (X-linked recessive), so it predominantly affects males (who have only one X chromosome), while females are usually carriers. Sickle cell anaemia, on the other hand, is caused by a mutation in the beta-globin gene located on chromosome 11 (autosomal recessive), affecting both males and females equally. The second difference is in phenotypic expression: in Haemophilia, heterozygous females (carriers) are phenotypically normal, whereas in sickle cell anaemia, heterozygous individuals show a mild form called sickle cell trait, demonstrating partial expression.
questions.solution_hindi: हीमोफीलिया X-सहलग्न अप्रभावी विकार है — मुख्यतः पुरुष प्रभावित; महिलाएं वाहक। दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता स्वपिंडी अप्रभावी विकार है — दोनों लिंगों को समान रूप से प्रभावित करता है।

questions.text_english: Predation is referred to as a detrimental interaction. Explain any three positive roles, supported by an example each, that a predator plays in an ecosystem.

key_points: Role 1: Predators control prey population — prevent overgrazing/overcrowding. Example: wolves controlling deer population.
Role 2: Predators maintain species diversity by preventing competitive exclusion. Example: starfish predation on mussels keeps rocky intertidal diversity high.
Role 3: Energy transfer through trophic levels — predators channel energy up the food chain. Example: owls eating mice.

questions.solution: Although predation is considered a detrimental interaction for the prey, predators play several positive roles in maintaining ecosystem health. First, predators regulate prey population size, preventing overpopulation that could lead to overgrazing and habitat destruction. For example, wolves in Yellowstone control deer and elk populations, allowing vegetation to recover. Second, predators help maintain species diversity in a community by preventing any one prey species from becoming dominant and competitively excluding others. A classic example is the predation of mussels by starfish (Pisaster) in rocky intertidal zones — when starfish were removed, mussels dominated and reduced species diversity. Third, predation facilitates energy flow through trophic levels, sustaining food webs and ecosystem productivity.
questions.solution_hindi: परभक्षी पारितंत्र में तीन सकारात्मक भूमिकाएं निभाते हैं: (1) शिकार जीवों की संख्या नियंत्रित करना (जैसे भेड़िया हिरण की संख्या नियंत्रित करता है); (2) जैव-विविधता बनाए रखना — एक जाति को प्रभावी होने से रोककर; (3) ऊर्जा का पोषण स्तरों के माध्यम से प्रवाह करना।

sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between humoral immune response and cell-mediated immune response.

key_points: Humoral: mediated by B-lymphocytes, produces antibodies (immunoglobulins) circulating in blood/lymph, effective against extracellular pathogens.
Cell-mediated: mediated by T-lymphocytes (killer T-cells), no antibody production, effective against intracellular pathogens, transplanted organs, cancer cells.

sub_questions.solution: Humoral immune response is mediated by B-lymphocytes. When stimulated by an antigen, B-cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete specific antibodies (immunoglobulins) into the blood and lymph. This response is effective against extracellular pathogens such as bacteria and viruses in body fluids. Cell-mediated immune response (CMI) is mediated by T-lymphocytes, particularly cytotoxic T-cells (killer T-cells). These cells directly attack and destroy infected cells, cancer cells, and transplanted foreign cells without producing antibodies. CMI is effective against intracellular pathogens like viruses inside cells, and is also responsible for graft rejection.

sub_questions.text: एक प्रतिरक्षी अणु का व्यवस्थात्मक आरेख बना कर इसके किन्हीं चार भागों को नामांकित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a schematic diagram of an antibody molecule and label any four parts.

key_points: Four parts to label: Heavy chain, Light chain, Variable region (antigen-binding site), Constant region, Hinge region, Fc region, Fab region, Disulphide bonds

sub_questions.solution: An antibody (immunoglobulin) molecule has a Y-shaped structure composed of four polypeptide chains: two identical heavy (H) chains and two identical light (L) chains, linked by disulphide bonds. The four parts to label are: (1) Heavy chain — the longer polypeptide chain forming the stem and upper arms of the Y; (2) Light chain — the shorter polypeptide chain on the outer sides of the upper arms; (3) Variable region (antigen-binding site) — located at the tips of the Y arms, this region is unique for each antibody and binds the specific antigen; (4) Constant region — the lower portion which determines the class of antibody and mediates effector functions.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the mechanism of haplo-diploid pattern of sex determination with the help of a suitable example. Why is this pattern so called ?

key_points: Seen in honey bees (Apis mellifera): fertilised eggs (diploid, 2n=32) develop into females (queens/workers); unfertilised eggs (haploid, n=16) develop into males (drones) by parthenogenesis.
Called haplo-diploid because males are haploid and females are diploid.

sub_questions.solution: The haplo-diploid pattern of sex determination is seen in honey bees (Apis mellifera). In this system, sex is determined by the ploidy level of the individual. Fertilised eggs, which are diploid (2n = 32), develop into females — either queens or sterile worker bees depending on the diet during larval development. Unfertilised eggs, which are haploid (n = 16), develop into males (drones) by a process called parthenogenesis (development without fertilization). This pattern is called haplo-diploid because males are haploid (developed from unfertilised eggs) and females are diploid (developed from fertilised eggs). Drones produce sperms by mitosis (not meiosis) because they are already haploid.

sub_questions.text: टी.एस. मोर्गन तथा उनके साथियों ने अपने प्रयोगों के लिए ड्रॉसोफिला मेलानोगैस्टर पर काम किया। वे जिन परिणामों पर पहुँचे उनका उल्लेख कीजिए और समझाइए, कैसे।
sub_questions.text_english: T.S. Morgan and his colleagues worked with Drosophila melanogaster for their experiments. State the findings they arrived at and explain how.

key_points: Finding 1: Genes located on same chromosome tend to be inherited together (linkage) — they do not assort independently.
Finding 2: Linked genes can sometimes be separated by crossing over (recombination) during meiosis.
Finding 3: Genes are linearly arranged on chromosomes.

sub_questions.solution: Morgan and his colleagues worked with Drosophila melanogaster and their key finding was the concept of linkage and recombination. They observed that certain genes located on the same chromosome tended to be inherited together and did not show independent assortment as Mendel's law predicted — this phenomenon was called linkage. However, they also found that linked genes could be separated by the physical exchange of chromosomal segments during meiosis, a process called crossing over, which resulted in recombinant offspring. The frequency of recombination between two genes was used to estimate the distance between them on the chromosome, leading to the construction of chromosomal maps (linkage maps). Morgan's work thus established that genes are linearly arranged on chromosomes.

questions.text: "मानव रुधिर वर्ग (ABO वर्ग) की वंशागति बहुऐलीलता तथा सह-प्रभाविता (को-डोमिनेंस) का एक अच्छा उदाहरण है।" कथन की न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Human blood group (ABO group) inheritance is a good example of multiple allelism and co-dominance." Justify the statement.

key_points: Multiple allelism: ABO is controlled by the I gene with three alleles — I^A, I^B, and i.
Co-dominance: In blood group AB (genotype I^A I^B), both alleles are expressed simultaneously — both A and B antigens are present on RBC surface.
Dominance: Both I^A and I^B are dominant over i (recessive).

questions.solution: Human ABO blood group inheritance justifies both multiple allelism and co-dominance. It demonstrates multiple allelism because the ABO blood group system is controlled by a single gene (gene I) that has three alleles in the population: I^A, I^B, and i. Although any individual can carry only two alleles, three alleles exist in the population, making it an example of multiple allelism. It demonstrates co-dominance because in individuals with genotype I^A I^B (blood group AB), both alleles are expressed simultaneously — the I^A allele codes for antigen A and the I^B allele codes for antigen B, and both antigens are present on the surface of red blood cells. Neither allele is dominant over the other; instead, they are co-dominant. The allele i is recessive to both I^A and I^B.

key_points: Named 'in vitro' (Latin: in glass) because fertilization occurs outside the body in a lab dish/glass vessel, not inside the body.
Importance: Helps infertile couples conceive; used when fallopian tubes are blocked; widely used assisted reproductive technology.

sub_questions.solution: IVF is called 'in vitro' fertilization because the word 'in vitro' is Latin for 'in glass', referring to the fact that fertilization occurs outside the living body in a glass laboratory dish or test tube, rather than inside the female reproductive tract. The resulting embryo (test tube baby) is then transferred to the uterus. Its importance lies in helping couples who are infertile due to various reasons — such as blocked fallopian tubes, low sperm count, or unexplained infertility — to achieve pregnancy. It is the most widely used assisted reproductive technology (ART) worldwide.

sub_questions.text_english: Distinguish between GIFT and ZIFT.

key_points: GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer): unfertilised eggs (ova) collected from donor and transferred into the fallopian tube of the recipient along with sperms; fertilization occurs inside the fallopian tube.
ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer): fertilization occurs outside (IVF) and the resulting zygote or early embryo is transferred into the fallopian tube (not the uterus directly).

sub_questions.solution: GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer) involves the transfer of unfertilised ova (eggs) collected from a donor, along with sperms, directly into the fallopian tube of the recipient female. Fertilization occurs naturally inside the fallopian tube. ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer) differs in that fertilization is first carried out outside the body (in vitro), and the resulting zygote or early-stage embryo (up to 8-cell stage) is then transferred into the fallopian tube of the recipient. Thus, in GIFT gametes are transferred, while in ZIFT it is the zygote/early embryo that is transferred into the fallopian tube.

In 1981, the health workers of United States of America had become aware of the increased frequency of Kaposi's sarcoma, cancer of the skin and blood vessels and another disease pneumocystis pneumonia, a respiratory infection caused by a protozoan. Both these diseases were very rare in the general population, but occurred frequently in more severely "immunosuppressed" individuals. This led to the recognition of the immune system disorder that was named Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

sub_questions.text_english: Name the group of cells the HIV attacks after gaining entry into the human body and write the various events that occur within this cell.

key_points: HIV attacks helper T-lymphocytes (T4 or CD4+ cells / macrophages).

Events: HIV enters cell, reverse transcriptase makes DNA from viral RNA, viral DNA integrates into host chromosome, viral proteins and RNA are synthesised, new virions bud off, destroying the T-helper cell.

sub_questions.solution: After entering the human body, HIV primarily attacks the helper T-lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells / T4 cells) and macrophages. Within the helper T-cell, the following events occur: the HIV uses its reverse transcriptase enzyme to make a DNA copy from its RNA genome (reverse transcription). This viral DNA then integrates into the host cell's chromosome, forming a provirus. The provirus remains latent initially and then becomes active, using the host cell's machinery to produce viral RNA and viral proteins. New virions are assembled and bud off from the infected cell, destroying the helper T-cell in the process. This progressive destruction of helper T-cells leads to a decrease in the number of T-helper cells, severely compromising the immune system.

key_points: Diagnostic test: ELISA — Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay
Treatment: Anti-retroviral therapy (ART) using drugs like zidovudine (AZT); no complete cure; drugs slow progression.

sub_questions.solution: The diagnostic test used for detecting AIDS is ELISA, which stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. This test detects the presence of HIV antibodies in the blood of the patient. A confirmed positive ELISA result is further validated by the Western Blot test. At present, AIDS has no complete cure. The available treatment is Anti-Retroviral Therapy (ART), which involves a combination of anti-retroviral drugs such as zidovudine (AZT), lamivudine, and others. These drugs inhibit viral replication, slow the progression of AIDS, and improve the quality and length of life of the patient, but do not completely eliminate the virus from the body.

अथवा: "एड्स से पीड़ित रोगी इस रोग के कारण नहीं मरता परन्तु किसी अन्य संक्रमण के कारण उसकी मृत्यु होती है।" कथन की न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Mention any two steps suggested by WHO for preventing the spread of this disease.

OR: "A patient suffering from AIDS does not die of this disease but from some other infection." Justify the statement.

key_points: WHO steps: (1) Use of disposable needles and syringes; (2) Practice safe sex / use of condoms; (3) Screening donated blood; (4) Awareness campaigns.

OR justification: HIV destroys helper T-cells, collapsing the immune system; patient cannot fight even minor infections like Pneumocystis pneumonia or tuberculosis, and dies from these secondary opportunistic infections, not directly from HIV.

sub_questions.solution:
Two steps suggested by WHO to prevent the spread of AIDS are: first, the use of disposable syringes and needles to prevent transmission through contaminated blood during injections; and second, promoting safe sex practices including the use of condoms, which reduces the risk of sexual transmission of HIV. Other measures include screening donated blood and blood products before transfusion, and conducting public awareness campaigns to educate people about routes of HIV transmission.

Alternate answer (OR): An AIDS patient does not die directly from the HIV infection but from opportunistic infections — this statement is justified because HIV specifically destroys the helper T-lymphocytes (CD4+ cells) over time, progressively weakening the immune system. When the CD4+ cell count falls below a critical level, the immune system is no longer able to fight even normally harmless pathogens. The patient then becomes susceptible to a wide range of opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis pneumonia, tuberculosis, Toxoplasma encephalitis, and various fungal infections. It is ultimately one of these secondary infections that causes death, not HIV itself directly.

Spermatogenesis is an important primary sex characteristic in humans and all other vertebrates. The process is coordinated and controlled under the influence of hormones. It starts with the onset of puberty in humans and thereafter continues. The primordial cells within the embryonic testis which differentiate into spermatogonia are the precursors of the sperms. These are located at the outer walls of the seminiferous tubules where the process of spermatogenesis proceeds.

sub_questions.text_english:
State the site of action of FSH in the testes and describe its action thereafter.

OR: Describe the role of LH in the process of spermatogenesis.

key_points: FSH acts on Sertoli cells (sustentacular cells) of seminiferous tubules; stimulates Sertoli cells to secrete factors/nutrients that aid spermatogenesis.
OR: LH acts on Leydig cells (interstitial cells) and stimulates them to secrete androgens (testosterone), which in turn stimulate and maintain spermatogenesis.

sub_questions.solution:
In the testes, FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) acts on the Sertoli cells (also called sustentacular cells or nurse cells) located within the seminiferous tubules. Upon stimulation by FSH, the Sertoli cells secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP) and various nutrients and paracrine factors that are essential for nourishing the developing spermatocytes and spermatids. FSH thus plays a crucial supportive and structural role in spermatogenesis by maintaining the blood-testis barrier and the microenvironment necessary for sperm development.

Alternate answer (OR): LH (Luteinizing Hormone) acts on the Leydig cells (interstitial cells of Leydig) located in the connective tissue between the seminiferous tubules. LH stimulates the Leydig cells to synthesise and secrete androgens, primarily testosterone. Testosterone then acts on the Sertoli cells and the developing germ cells within the seminiferous tubules to stimulate and sustain all stages of spermatogenesis, from the division of spermatogonia to the final maturation of spermatozoa.

Name the cells and their products which undergo:
(i) Mitosis and Differentiation
(ii) Meiosis I and Meiosis II
during the process of spermatogenesis.

key_points: (i) Spermatogonia undergo mitosis → produce primary spermatocytes; spermatids undergo differentiation (spermiogenesis) → produce spermatozoa.

sub_questions.solution: During spermatogenesis: (i) Mitosis and Differentiation — Spermatogonia (2n) undergo repeated mitotic divisions to produce more spermatogonia and eventually primary spermatocytes. (ii) Meiosis I and Meiosis II — Primary spermatocytes (2n) undergo the first meiotic division (Meiosis I) to produce two secondary spermatocytes (n). Each secondary spermatocyte then undergoes the second meiotic division (Meiosis II) to produce four spermatids (n), which eventually differentiate into mature spermatozoa.

key_points: Cells must be made competent because the cell wall and plasma membrane are barriers that prevent DNA entry.

Calcium ion method: bacterial cells treated with ice-cold CaCl2 solution to increase permeability of cell wall; then incubated with recombinant DNA on ice; heat shock (42°C briefly) causes DNA to enter the cell.

sub_questions.solution: A cell must be made competent to take up an alien (foreign) DNA because under normal physiological conditions, bacterial cell walls and plasma membranes act as barriers, preventing the entry of large DNA molecules. Competence refers to the physiological state that allows a cell to take up external DNA. To make a bacterial cell competent using calcium ions, the bacteria are first treated with a divalent cation solution — specifically ice-cold calcium chloride (CaCl2). The calcium ions alter the cell wall and membrane, increasing their permeability to DNA by neutralising negative charges. The recombinant DNA (plasmid) is then incubated with these treated cells on ice. This is followed by a brief heat shock treatment (placing cells at 42°C for a short period), which facilitates the entry of recombinant DNA into the cells. The cells are then placed back on ice to recover before being plated on antibiotic medium to select transformants.

sub_questions.text: (1) जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी में जेल वैद्युत कण-संचलन का महत्त्व लिखिए। (2) उस सिद्धान्त की व्याख्या कीजिए जिस पर यह तकनीक कार्य करती है। (3) इस तकनीक में इथीडियम ब्रोमाइड का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (1) State the importance of gel electrophoresis in biotechnology. (2) Explain the principle on which this technique works. (3) Mention why ethidium bromide is used in this technique.

key_points: Importance: Used to separate DNA fragments of different sizes; to check restriction digestion; to identify and isolate specific DNA fragments for cloning.
Principle: DNA is negatively charged; under electric field in agarose gel, DNA migrates towards anode; smaller fragments migrate faster/further than larger fragments.
Ethidium bromide: intercalating fluorescent dye that binds to DNA; under UV light the DNA bands fluoresce orange, making them visible for detection and photography.

sub_questions.solution: (1) Gel electrophoresis is extremely important in biotechnology for the separation, identification, and isolation of DNA fragments of different sizes produced by restriction enzyme digestion. It is used to verify successful cloning, to prepare DNA fragments for further manipulation, and to analyse PCR products. (2) The technique works on the principle that DNA molecules carry a net negative charge due to the phosphate backbone. When an electric current is applied, DNA fragments migrate through an agarose gel matrix towards the positively charged anode. The gel acts as a molecular sieve — smaller DNA fragments experience less resistance and migrate faster, travelling a greater distance, while larger fragments move more slowly and remain closer to the wells. This results in the separation of fragments by size. (3) Ethidium bromide is used as a fluorescent stain that intercalates between the stacked nitrogenous bases of the DNA double helix. When the gel is exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, the DNA-ethidium bromide complexes emit bright orange fluorescence, making the DNA bands visible for detection, photography, and quantification.

sub_questions.text: बीटी (Bt) कपास के पौधे को गोलक शलभ कृमि के लिए प्रतिरोधी किस प्रकार बनाया गया ? व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How was Bt cotton plant made resistant to bollworm ? Explain.

key_points: Bt cotton was made resistant by inserting the cry genes (specifically cry1Ac and cry2Ab) from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis into the cotton plant genome using Agrobacterium tumefaciens as a vector.
These genes encode Cry proteins (crystal proteins / delta-endotoxins) that are toxic to bollworm larvae.

sub_questions.solution: Bt cotton was made resistant to bollworm by introducing specific genes called cry genes (crystalline insecticidal protein genes) from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis into the cotton plant. The genes used are cry1Ac and cry2Ab. These genes were transferred using Agrobacterium tumefaciens as a vector in the process of plant transformation. The transgenic Bt cotton plants now carry these cry genes in every cell, and they express the Cry proteins (also called delta-endotoxins or crystal proteins). When bollworm larvae feed on any part of the Bt cotton plant, they ingest these Cry proteins, which are toxic specifically to insect larvae, leading to their death.

sub_questions.text: बीटी (Bt) कपास के पौधों को खाने वाले गोलक शलभ कृमियों के मरने की क्रियाविधि का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the mechanism that leads to the death of bollworms feeding on Bt cotton plants.

key_points: Cry proteins are produced as inactive pro-toxins in the plant.
When ingested by bollworm larvae, the alkaline pH of the insect gut activates the pro-toxin.
Active toxin binds to specific receptors on the epithelial cells of the midgut, creating pores that disrupt ion balance and cause cell lysis.
Larva stops feeding, becomes paralysed, and dies.

sub_questions.solution: The mechanism of death of bollworms feeding on Bt cotton plants involves the following steps. The Cry proteins (delta-endotoxins) are produced in an inactive form called pro-toxins within the plant cells. When a bollworm larva feeds on the Bt cotton plant, it ingests the plant material containing these inactive pro-toxins. Inside the midgut of the insect larva, the highly alkaline pH (around pH 9-10) activates the pro-toxin by solubilizing and partially digesting the crystal protein. The activated Cry toxin then binds specifically to receptor proteins on the surface of the epithelial cells lining the insect's midgut. This binding causes the toxin to insert into the cell membrane, creating ion channels or pores. These pores disrupt the ionic balance of the epithelial cells, causing them to swell and lyse (burst). The midgut epithelium is destroyed, the larva stops feeding, becomes paralysed, and ultimately dies.

sub_questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी में वर्तिकाग्र पर परागकण के जनित होने से लेकर द्विनिषेचन तक के प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए तथा अंतिम उत्पादों की सूत्रगुणता का उल्लेख कीजिए। इस प्रक्रम में सहाय कोशिकाओं की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the process of double fertilization in an angiosperm starting from the germination of pollen grains on the stigma, mentioning the ploidy of the end products formed. State the role of synergids during the course of the process.

key_points: Pollen grain germinates on stigma, pollen tube grows through style guided by synergids.
Pollen tube carries two male gametes (n) into the embryo sac through one synergid.
First fertilization: one male gamete (n) fuses with egg cell (n) → zygote (2n) — syngamy.
Second fertilization: other male gamete (n) fuses with diploid secondary nucleus (2n) → primary endosperm nucleus (3n) — triple fusion.
End products: zygote (2n) → embryo; PEN (3n) → endosperm. Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms.
Synergids: guide pollen tube entry, secrete chemotropic substances, help in release of male gametes.

sub_questions.solution: When a pollen grain lands on the stigma of a compatible flower, it absorbs moisture and germinates to produce a pollen tube. The pollen tube grows through the style toward the ovule, guided by chemical signals secreted by the synergids. The pollen tube enters the embryo sac through the micropyle and typically penetrates one of the two synergids. The synergids play a crucial role by secreting chemotropic substances that attract and guide the pollen tube, and by facilitating the release of the two male gametes into the embryo sac after the pollen tube ruptures. Once inside the embryo sac, the two male gametes are released. One male gamete (haploid, n) fuses with the egg cell (haploid, n) in a process called syngamy to form the diploid zygote (2n), which will develop into the embryo. The second male gamete (n) fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (formed by the fusion of the two polar nuclei, 2n) in a process called triple fusion, producing the triploid primary endosperm nucleus or PEN (3n), which will develop into the endosperm. Since fertilization occurs twice, this process is called double fertilization and is a unique feature of angiosperms.

sub_questions.text: भ्रूणपोष का विकास भ्रूण के विकास से पहले होता है, क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does the development of endosperm precede that of the embryo ?

key_points: Endosperm develops before embryo to provide nourishment and nutrients required for the growth and development of the embryo.

sub_questions.solution: The development of endosperm precedes that of the embryo because the endosperm serves as the primary nutritive tissue that provides food, energy, and essential nutrients to the developing embryo. The embryo is a rapidly dividing and differentiating structure that requires a continuous supply of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and other nutrients. If the endosperm were to develop after the embryo, the embryo would have no nutritional support during its critical early stages of development. Therefore, the endosperm must be established first to act as a ready source of nourishment for the growing embryo.

sub_questions.text: उस स्थल का उल्लेख कीजिए जहाँ स्त्री (मानव मादा) में अंडाणु का निषेचन होता है। निषेचन प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए और उल्लेख कीजिए कि इस प्रक्रम में अनेक शुक्राणुओं के प्रवेश को कैसे रोका जाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention the site where fertilisation of the ovum occurs in a human female. Explain the process of fertilization and mention how polyspermy is prevented.

key_points: Site: Ampullary region of the fallopian tube (oviduct).
Process: sperm reaches secondary oocyte in ampulla, acrosomal reaction releases enzymes to penetrate zona pellucida, sperm fuses with egg membrane, triggers completion of meiosis II, forms zygote.
Prevention of polyspermy: zona reaction — cortical granules released on sperm entry change the zona pellucida, making it impenetrable to further sperms.

sub_questions.solution: In a human female, fertilization of the ovum occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube (oviduct). The process of fertilization begins when a sperm reaches the secondary oocyte. The acrosomal reaction occurs — enzymes stored in the acrosome (head of sperm) are released, which help the sperm to penetrate the zona pellucida (the transparent coat surrounding the egg). After the sperm contacts the plasma membrane of the egg, sperm-egg fusion occurs, which triggers the completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte, releasing the second polar body and forming the mature ovum. The haploid nuclei of the sperm and ovum fuse to form the diploid zygote. To prevent polyspermy (entry of more than one sperm), a zona reaction occurs immediately after the first sperm enters — cortical granules present just below the egg plasma membrane are released by exocytosis, and their contents modify the zona pellucida, hardening it into a fertilization membrane that is impenetrable to additional sperms.

sub_questions.text: भ्रूण की उस अवस्था का नाम लिखिए जिसमें उसका गर्भाशय में अंतरोपण होता है। स्त्री (मानव मादा) में अंतरोपण प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the embryonic stage that gets implanted in the uterus. Explain the process of implantation in a human female.

key_points: Embryonic stage: Blastocyst.

Implantation process: blastocyst reaches uterus 4-5 days after fertilization, zona pellucida degenerates, trophoblast cells of blastocyst attach to uterine endometrium, trophoblast penetrates endometrium and establishes contact with maternal blood supply.

sub_questions.solution: The embryonic stage that gets implanted in the uterus is the blastocyst. After fertilization, the zygote undergoes cleavage divisions as it travels down the fallopian tube. By the time it reaches the uterus (about 4-5 days after fertilization), it has developed into a blastocyst — a hollow ball of cells consisting of an outer trophoblast layer and an inner cell mass (embryoblast). The zona pellucida degenerates (hatching of blastocyst), and the trophoblast cells come in direct contact with the uterine endometrium. The blastocyst adheres to the endometrial wall of the uterus, typically in the posterior wall of the upper uterus. The trophoblast cells then proliferate and penetrate the endometrial epithelium and stroma by enzymatic digestion. The inner cell mass differentiates and the blastocyst becomes embedded within the endometrium — this is called implantation. The trophoblast eventually develops into the placenta, establishing the nutritional and hormonal connection between the embryo and the mother.

questions.instruction_line: अथवा (OR): (ख) आनुवंशिक पदार्थ की खोज के लिए ग्रीफिथ द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग की व्याख्या कीजिए। इसके परिणामस्वरूप वह जिस निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचे उसे लिखिए। एवेरी, मैकलिओड एवं मैककाटी ने ग्रीफिथ के "आनुवंशिक पदार्थ" की जीव-रासायनिक प्रकृति को स्थापित (का निर्धारण) कैसे किया ?

sub_questions.text: (i) मेंडल के स्वतंत्र अपव्यूहन का नियम लिखिए। (ii) इस नियम की व्याख्या मटर के पुष्प के रंग तथा पुष्प की पौधे पर स्थिति के संदर्भ में दो विषमयुग्मजी जनक पौधों के बीच क्रॉस के उदाहरण द्वारा पनेट वर्ग बना कर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) State Mendel's law of independent assortment. (ii) Explain this law using a cross between two heterozygous parents of pea plants with respect to flower colour and flower position using Punnett Square.

key_points: Law: When two pairs of contrasting characters are considered together in a cross, the alleles of different genes assort (segregate) independently of each other during gamete formation, giving a 9:3:3:1 ratio in F2.
Cross: Flower colour (Violet/V dominant, White/v recessive) × Flower position (Axial/A dominant, Terminal/a recessive). Both parents heterozygous: VvAa × VvAa.
Gametes: VA, Va, vA, va (each parent produces 4 types of gametes).
F2 Punnett square (4×4) gives 16 combinations: 9 V_A_ (violet axial) : 3 V_aa (violet terminal) : 3 vvA_ (white axial) : 1 vvaa (white terminal) = 9:3:3:1.

sub_questions.solution:
Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment states that when two pairs of contrasting characters are considered simultaneously in a cross, the factors (alleles) for each pair of characters assort independently of the factors for the other pair of characters during the formation of gametes. This results in new combinations of traits in the offspring.

To explain this law, consider a dihybrid cross in pea plants for flower colour (violet V is dominant over white v) and flower position (axial A is dominant over terminal a). Both parents are dihybrid (heterozygous for both traits): VvAa × VvAa. Each parent produces four types of gametes in equal proportions: VA, Va, vA, and va. A 4×4 Punnett square is constructed using these four gamete types for each parent, giving 16 possible combinations.

The F2 phenotypic ratio is 9 Violet Axial (V_A_) : 3 Violet Terminal (V_aa) : 3 White Axial (vvA_) : 1 White Terminal (vvaa), a classic 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio. The appearance of two new combinations — violet terminal and white axial — which were not present in the parents confirms that the two genes assorted independently of each other, justifying Mendel's law.

sub_questions.text: आनुवंशिक पदार्थ की खोज के लिए ग्रीफिथ द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग की व्याख्या कीजिए। इसके परिणामस्वरूप वह जिस निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचे उसे लिखिए। एवेरी, मैकलिओड एवं मैककाटी ने ग्रीफिथ के 'आनुवंशिक पदार्थ' की जीव-रासायनिक प्रकृति को स्थापित कैसे किया ?
sub_questions.text_english: Explain Griffith's experiment conducted in search of genetic material and write the conclusion he arrived at. How did Avery, MacLeod and McCarty establish the biochemical nature of the 'Genetic Material' identified by Griffith ?

key_points: Griffith's experiment (1928): used Streptococcus pneumoniae — virulent S-strain (smooth, capsule) and non-virulent R-strain (rough, no capsule).

Injected: live S → mice died; live R → mice survived; heat-killed S → mice survived; live R + heat-killed S → mice died. Conclusion: some 'transforming principle' from dead S-strain transformed R-strain into virulent S-strain.

Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1944): purified the transforming principle from S-strain. Treated with protease (protein destroyed) — still transformed; RNase (RNA destroyed) — still transformed; DNase (DNA destroyed) — transformation abolished. Conclusion: DNA is the genetic material (transforming principle).

sub_questions.solution:
Frederick Griffith (1928) conducted his famous experiment using two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae — the virulent S-strain (smooth colony, encapsulated) and the non-virulent R-strain (rough colony, no capsule). He observed that when live S-strain bacteria were injected into mice, the mice died. When live R-strain bacteria were injected, the mice survived. When heat-killed S-strain was injected, mice survived. Most significantly, when a mixture of live R-strain and heat-killed S-strain was injected, mice died, and live S-strain bacteria could be recovered from the dead mice. Griffith concluded that some 'transforming principle' from the dead S-strain bacteria had transformed the living R-strain into virulent S-strain, a process he called transformation.

Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1944) then worked to identify the biochemical nature of Griffith's transforming principle. They purified different macromolecules (proteins, RNA, DNA) from the S-strain and tested each separately for transformation ability. They found that treatment with protease (which destroys proteins) did not prevent transformation. Treatment with RNase (which destroys RNA) also did not prevent transformation. However, treatment with DNase (which destroys DNA) completely abolished transformation — R-strain cells could no longer be transformed into S-strain. This conclusively proved that DNA, and not protein or RNA, was the transforming principle — that is, the genetic material.
